name: 140. Pre-auth request limits: compressed body bounds and malformed realtime SDP (request-limits)
description: Three request-size limits on routes reachable before authentication. (1) Request decompression runs ahead of routing and auth; its zstd decoder now caps the declared back-reference window and content size, so a tiny body whose frame header declares a 512 MiB window is answered 413 at once instead of making the process reserve that window. (2) The realtime calls route hands the request body to the SDP parser; an offer with an empty simulcast rid segment is answered with an HTTP status (client error when the offer is rejected, bad gateway when the stubbed upstream is reached) rather than dropping the connection, and the gateway stays up. (3) A liveness probe after the malformed offer confirms the gateway still serves. No case opens with a status-skipping guard: every unexpected status fails the assertion. The zstd case sends a fixture file body so the exact nine bytes reach the server unaltered.
